clue.text: Practise how to don a glove

definitions.meaning: to regain skill through practice, the idiom for getting back into form
literally, slipping a hand inside a glove

explanation.surface: A tongue-in-cheek instruction on rehearsing the art of wearing gloves.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to regain a skill by practising; read literally it describes pushing a hand into a glove.

clue.text: Pets distraught Giselle losing the French and taking in backward British

indicators.note: taking in means one piece is put inside the other
distraught suggests someone in a state, so the letters are thrown into disorder
losing tells us to drop letters from the name Giselle

parts.note: le is the French masculine word for the

indicators.note: backward tells us to read the abbreviation from right to left

explanation.surface: A girl called Giselle is upset about her pets, and something French and British is involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' removes LE from GISELLE, leaving GISEL; 'distraught' shuffles it to GEILS; 'backward' turns BR into RB, and 'taking in' places RB after GE.
explanation.definitionFit: These small burrowing rodents are commonly kept as household animals.

clue.text: Give it at whirl to see if the cap fit

definitions.text: Give it at whirl to see if the cap fit

parts.words: Give it at whirl to see if the cap fit
parts.note: the clue (printed with OCR slips for 'a whirl' and 'fits') describes testing a cap by putting it on your head

explanation.surface: Advice to have a go at something, as the proverb about the cap fitting suggests.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan text reads 'at whirl' and 'fit' where the setter wrote 'a whirl' and 'fits'. The phrase means both to attempt something and to put on clothing to test the fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Testing whether headwear suits you means placing it on; the phrase also means having a go.

clue.text: Storage bags for rifles

definitions.meaning: large coarse bags used for holding coal, flour or potatoes
here a verb: ransacks or plunders, as an army pillages a town

explanation.surface: A query about bags used to store guns.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse bags are this, and to plunder a town is to do this to it.

clue.text: See there the olive grove of "(Milton)

definitions.text: See there the olive grove of "(Milton)

parts.words: See there the olive grove of "(Milton)
parts.note: a quotation from Milton's Paradise Regained with its last word missing, the name of Plato's school near Athens

explanation.surface: A line of Milton describing an olive grove, with its final word left blank.
explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank quotation: Milton's line ends 'the olive grove of Academe', the garden where Plato taught.
explanation.definitionFit: Plato's school stood in an olive grove outside Athens, and the word now names the academic world.

clue.text: The hem has been raised to look really smart

definitions.meaning: read literally, a frock lifted higher
to wear formal or fancy clothes for an occasion

explanation.surface: A shortened hemline makes someone look very chic.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as frock lifted, a raised hem fits it; idiomatically it means to put on one's best clothes.

clue.text: Husband supports personality creating ecological centre

indicators.note: in a down entry the piece that supports sits underneath the other one

parts.note: a person's nature is their character or personality
to husband resources is to conserve or reserve them

explanation.surface: A married man propping up a strong character, said to create an ecological centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Husband' looks like a noun; here it is the verb meaning to save or conserve. In a down clue 'supports' puts RESERVE below NATURE.
explanation.definitionFit: A protected area where wildlife and habitats are conserved is an ecological site.

clue.text: Your argument reflected concern

indicators.note: as in a mirror, the whole run of letters appears backwards

parts.note: a row is a noisy quarrel or argument

explanation.surface: A remark that your quarrel showed some anxiety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflected' turns YRROW round as one run.
explanation.definitionFit: Anxiety or unease about something is a synonym of the noun.

clue.text: Supervisory duty given to sentries

parts.note: a legal term for a brief to observe proceedings, read as instructions to guards who keep watch

explanation.surface: Guards being handed their orders to oversee something.
explanation.walkthrough: In law the phrase means a barrister's instruction to observe a case on behalf of someone not directly involved; the clue reads it as orders for lookouts.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawyer's remit to monitor a case without taking part is a supervisory role; sentries' orders would be to keep watch.

clue.text: A Schubert composition? Capital!

indicators.note: a musical composition by Schubert suggests letters put together in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Is this a piece of music by Schubert? Splendid!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital!' looks like an exclamation of approval, but it is the definition: a capital city. 'composition' rearranges A SCHUBERT.
explanation.definitionFit: The Romanian seat of government is a national capital city.

clue.text: Covering a book is obligatory

definitions.meaning: the cover and spine that hold a volume together
a contract that is legally enforceable

explanation.surface: A statement that putting a cover on a book is compulsory.
explanation.definitionFit: The cover of a volume is this, and an agreement that must be honoured is also this.

clue.text: He's first in race after the leader

indicators.note: after means the following piece comes later than the first letter
the leader of the word the is its opening letter
in places one piece within the other

parts.note: ran is a verb for raced
1st, written IST, is the abbreviation for first

explanation.surface: Someone finishing top in a race after trailing the frontrunner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts IST (1st) inside RAN, giving RISTAN; 'after the leader' places that after T, the first letter of 'the'. The definition is just 'He': a man, the knight of Cornish legend.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's name: the Arthurian knight who loved Isolde.

clue.text: Poles housed by Nazi minister who wrote poetry

indicators.note: housed by means the first piece is placed inside the second

parts.note: Albert Speer was Hitler's armaments minister
N and S are the North and South poles

explanation.surface: Polish people being sheltered by a Nazi official who wrote verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' wants to be people from Poland; it is the two magnetic poles, N and S, which 'housed by' puts inside SPEER.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Spenser, author of The Faerie Queene, was an Elizabethan poet.

clue.text: Like a pipe in garden of those needing water

indicators.note: of signals that the answer is part of the following words, taken out of them

explanation.surface: Something resembling a garden hose for plants that need watering.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'tHOSE Needing'. The old plural of a garden pipe word, also used for breeches or stockings; 'water' completes the garden picture.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic plural of hose, the flexible tube used for watering lawns.

clue.text: Ill-humoured painter disposed to hold me back

indicators.note: to hold means one piece wraps round the other
disposed means arranged, so the letters of painter are set out afresh
back says the word me is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A grumpy artist inclined to keep the speaker at arm's length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposed' rearranges PAINTER to INATPER; 'back' turns ME to EM; 'to hold' puts EM inside, after INAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a bad mood or angry is the meaning of the phrase.

clue.text: Leave a troupe no comeback

parts.note: a band is a group or troupe of performers

indicators.note: comeback tells us the word no returns, written backwards

explanation.surface: A performing group gets no chance of a return show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comeback' turns NO into ON at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To desert or forsake something is a synonym for this verb.

clue.text: Lost again recollecting times gone by

definitions.text: Lost again recollecting times gone by

indicators.note: read as re-collecting, the letters of lost again are gathered up anew

explanation.surface: Someone lost in memories of the past once more.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a wistful longing for the past, while 'recollecting' (re-collecting) rearranges LOST AGAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentimental longing for the past is what memory of bygone days brings.

clue.text: I am also involved in Africa

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are mixed together

explanation.surface: Someone saying they too are caught up in African affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Africa' stands for a country there, as a crossword shorthand; 'involved' rearranges I AM ALSO.
explanation.definitionFit: This Horn of Africa country is on the continent's eastern coast.

clue.text: Getting fed up around midday

parts.note: fed up looks like annoyed, but means eating, at the time of day noon falls

explanation.surface: Someone growing irritated around noon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fed up' suggests exasperation; read literally it is being given a meal at noon.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking the midday meal is to be out eating at noon.

clue.text: Phoney is made to go back into the coach

indicators.note: into means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a coach is a bus

indicators.note: back means the word go is read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written before it is turned

explanation.surface: A fraud is forced to return to the coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns GO to OG, and 'into' places it inside BUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fake or counterfeit is a synonym.

clue.text: Extravagant publicity to create cities in the air

definitions.meaning: hype or promotion ahead of an event
to develop an area with tall buildings

explanation.surface: Lavish advertising for a scheme to build cities in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Hype before a launch is one sense; constructing towering urban areas is the other.

clue.text: Bought fine feathers when depressed

definitions.meaning: acquired soft plumage, such as that used in pillows

explanation.surface: Someone who purchased fine plumage while feeling low.
explanation.definitionFit: Acquiring soft plumage reads one way; feeling glum is the idiom.

clue.text: Blunders of a Dickensian beadle

definitions.meaning: makes clumsy mistakes; verb, third person
belonging to Mr Bumble, the beadle in Oliver Twist

explanation.surface: The mistakes made by a parish beadle from a Dickens novel.
explanation.walkthrough: A beadle was a minor parish officer; Dickens's beadle in Oliver Twist is Mr Bumble, so 'of' him is the possessive form.
explanation.definitionFit: To stumble clumsily is one sense; the possessive of Mr Bumble from Oliver Twist is the other.

clue.text: The material didn't stand out

definitions.meaning: sat and stayed indoors rather than standing outside

explanation.surface: A fabric that was unremarkable.
explanation.definitionFit: A glossy fabric is one sense; taking a seat indoors rather than standing outside is the other.

clue.text: Crack appearing in the German fishing boat

indicators.note: appearing in means one piece shows up inside the other

parts.note: der is a German word for the
a rift is a crack or split

explanation.surface: A split shows up in a fishing vessel from Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat that fishes with drift nets is so called.

clue.text: One weapon David had not brought back from London area

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
David killed Goliath with a sling

indicators.note: brought back means the word not is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A person bringing a sling back from London, as David had not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' turns NOT into TON.
explanation.definitionFit: A borough in north London is a district of the capital.

clue.text: The same unique family portrayed by Blackmore

parts.note: do, short for ditto, means the same
one means single or unique

explanation.surface: A singular clan depicted by the novelist Blackmore.
explanation.walkthrough: DO is short for ditto, used in lists to mean 'the same'.
explanation.definitionFit: R. D. Blackmore's novel Lorna Doone is about an outlaw clan on Exmoor.

clue.text: Flambe's a fad

parts.note: a dish set alight in cookware produces a brief blaze, and a short-lived craze is described by the same idiom

explanation.surface: A claim that flaming dishes are just a passing trend.
explanation.walkthrough: A flambé produces a sudden flare in cookware; the idiom describes a short-lived success.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief burst that comes to nothing is likened to a powder flare in an old musket.
